units.name: My Family and My Home
units.summary: Who lives in a home, and how people in a family help each other.

topics.name: My Family
topics.summary: The people in a family, and the jobs they share at home.

objectives.text: Name the people who live in a home.
Say one job that people share at home.
Say why families help each other.

keyTerms.definition: The people who care for you and who you belong to.
The place where you live and sleep.
To do something together, or give some to someone else.

sections.heading: What you will learn
sections.body:
You will learn who is in a family.

You will learn about jobs at home.

You will learn why families help each other.

sections.heading: Families are not all the same
sections.body:
Some children live with a mother and a father.

Some live with one parent.

Some live with a grandmother, or an aunt, or an older sister.

Some homes have many children. Some have one.

All of these are families.

A family is not one shape. A family is the people who care for you.

sections.heading: Jobs at home
sections.body:
A home has work to do every day.

Someone fetches water.

Someone cooks the food.

Someone washes the clothes.

Someone sweeps the floor.

Someone looks after the small children.

If one person did all of it, that person would be very tired. So the work is shared.

Even a small child can help. Carrying a cup. Holding a baby's hand.
sections.example:
One evening in a home.

The sun is going down. There is a lot to do before dark.

The older brother fetches the water.

The mother starts the fire and cooks.

The small sister sweeps the step. It takes her a long time, but she does it.

The grandmother holds the baby so the mother can cook.

Four people. Four jobs. Everyone eats.

If nobody had fetched water, nobody would have eaten. Every job mattered.

sections.heading: Why families help each other
sections.body:
Nobody can do everything alone.

A baby cannot cook.

A small child cannot carry a heavy bucket.

Someone who is sick cannot sweep.

So people do what they can, and others do the rest.

That is what helping means. You do your part. Someone else does theirs.

sections.heading: Try it yourself
sections.body:
Think about your own home. Answer out loud.

1. Who lives in your home?

2. Name one job that gets done at your home every day.

3. Who does that job?

4. What is one job you could help with?

5. Why is it better when the work is shared?

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body:
• A family is the people who care for you.
• Families come in many shapes.
• A home has work to do every day.
• The work is shared, so nobody is too tired.
• Everyone can help with something.

questions.question: Which of these is a family?
options: Only a mother, a father and their children
Any people who care for each other and live together
Only people who have the same job
questions.explanation: Families come in many shapes. Some children live with one parent, some with a grandmother, some with an aunt. All of these are families. A family is the people who care for you.

questions.question: Why do people in a home share the work?
options: So one person does not have to do everything
questions.explanation: There is a lot to do every day — water, cooking, washing, sweeping. If one person did all of it they would be very tired, and some jobs would not get done. Sharing means everyone does a part.
